topic: Sharp minimax estimation of the unrestricted optimal treatment-policy value with high-dimensional discrete confounders: for iid (X,A,Y), X in [d], binary A,Y, consistency, conditional exchangeability, and fixed overlap epsilon, target V*(P)=sum_x p_x max{mu_0x,mu_1x}; prove minimax MSE equivalent up to epsilon-dependent constants to 1/n+d/(n log n) uniformly for d<=rho_epsilon n log n, with parametric risk only through d=O(log n) and consistency iff d=o(n log n); construct a computable sample-split mass-and-tie diagonal-adaptive estimator using ratio plug-in only on pilot-certified heavy regions separated from the treatment-effect tie diagonal, and best multivariate polynomial/factorial-moment estimation of the homogeneous ratio-absolute-contrast on every near-tie region including heavy cells plus sparse overlap-cone regions; match it with a randomized equal-propensity symmetric-Bernoulli fuzzy-prior lower bound. This is a scalar oracle optimal-value frontier, not learned-policy regret or fixed-dimensional honest-CI adaptation.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the unrestricted binary-treatment oracle value over a d-cell confounder alphabet has minimax MSE comparable to 1/n+d/(n log n) under fixed overlap, with root-n risk only through d=O(log n) and consistency exactly when d=o(n log n).

source_refs.claim: Derives high-dimensional discrete-covariate minimax bounds for linear causal means and ATE, but does not study the nonsmooth unrestricted optimal-policy value.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.claim: Proves n log n effective-sample-size enlargement for L1 distance between large-alphabet discrete distributions using multivariate approximation near the equality diagonal.
source_refs.author: Jiantao Jiao, Yanjun Han, Tsachy Weissman

source_refs.claim: Characterizes the pathwise-differentiability boundary of the unrestricted optimal value and identifies treatment-effect ties as the nonregular locus.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke, Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.excerpt: The calibration uses a polynomial approximation of phi on the overlap-restricted four-cell cone
The signed construction keeps the causal max functional positive while the signs conceal the alternatives

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest causal minimax result treats linear treatment-specific means, while the optimal value adds a cellwise absolute contrast. Under equal known propensity this resembles large-alphabet L1 distance, but observational propensities turn every cell contribution into a homogeneous ratio-absolute-contrast. The accepted ATE construction approximates inverse arm masses on an overlap cone and uses ratio plug-in on heavy cells; its first proof step fails here because the absolute-value cusp persists on the treatment-effect tie diagonal even inside heavy cells. A resolution therefore needs a joint mass-and-diagonal pilot partition, multivariate approximation on near-tie overlap-cone regions, covariance control for the factorial lift, and a causal fuzzy prior that hides signed contrasts while preserving overlap. Neither fixed-dimensional optimal-value inference nor existing L1 estimation supplies that combination.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching nonasymptotic upper and lower MSE bounds up to overlap-dependent constants, an explicit computable mass-and-tie diagonal-adaptive estimator, and a symmetric-Bernoulli fuzzy-prior converse establishing the d=O(log n) and d=o(n log n) thresholds.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the closest discrete-confounder minimax setup and turns sparse cell occupancy into a sharp causal estimation question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Many categorical confounder strata create unseen and low-count cells -> standard causal plug-ins accumulate occupancy and ratio error -> sharp minimax analysis reveals n log n information amplification for linear means -> determine the added global cost of the nonsmooth oracle maximum.

method_exemplars.technique: Use sample splitting to certify smooth versus diagonal regions, approximate the bivariate absolute difference near the diagonal, estimate polynomial monomials by factorial moments, and prove matching MSE bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The difficult part of the oracle value is an aggregate absolute contrast; the destination replaces two multinomial masses by homogeneous causal ratios on an overlap cone.

method_exemplars.technique: Poissonize discrete causal cells, decompose ratio-estimation risk by occupancy, and construct moment-matched causal priors that preserve exchangeability and overlap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact observed-data experiment and the causal lower-bound constraints that must be combined with the max functional's tie-diagonal loss.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple best polynomial approximation and unbiased factorial moments for the upper bound with moment-matched fuzzy priors obtained from approximation duality for the lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the proof architecture that converts a nonsmooth functional into an n log n consistency threshold on both sides of the minimax comparison.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the minimax MSE of the high-dimensional discrete optimal value over weighted margin classes that bound near-tie mass while permitting an explicit atom at exact treatment-effect ties.

source_refs.claim: Shows that the optimal value's pathwise differentiability depends on the law at strata where the treatment contrast is exactly zero.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke, Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.claim: Uses softmax smoothing and suboptimality-gap conditions for optimal-value inference, but does not derive growing-alphabet minimax point risk with exact tie atoms.
source_refs.author: Justin Whitehouse, Qizhao Chen, Morgane Austern, Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.claim: Uses a margin condition to sharpen value-reduction rates for structured treatment rules, but studies learned-rule regret rather than minimax estimation of the unrestricted scalar oracle value.
source_refs.author: Qi Xu, Haoda Fu, Annie Qu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.excerpt: The union contains an exact-tie Holder stratum and a near-tie Holder stratum
extension to arbitrary tie-mass bands, and the global adaptation diagram remain open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Margin assumptions currently control learned-policy regret or justify smoothing when nuisance functions are already estimable fast enough; the prior CausalSmith result instead gives a sparse randomized-sign confidence-length lower family in a smooth continuous-covariate model. None determines squared-error point risk when d-cell occupancy, unknown arm ratios, and an exact tie atom coexist. The first unrestricted proof step that changes is the approximation-bias sum: it must aggregate near-diagonal polynomial error against a weighted margin law rather than pay d times a worst-cell error. Its lower-bound counterpart must constrain the cell masses and signed mixture to satisfy the same margin and tie-atom conditions. Existing ordered-modulus and regret arguments do not yield that factorial-moment estimator or its matching risk.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching risk formula R(n,d,alpha,C,w0,epsilon) with explicit elbows and consistency thresholds, plus a margin-adaptive diagonal polynomial estimator and a constrained causal fuzzy-prior lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the optimal value as a maximum-type irregular functional and makes action-gap behavior the bridge between ties and regular estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The scalar optimal value is a maximum of causal scores -> the maximum is nondifferentiable near tied actions -> gap behavior controls smoothing bias and regularity -> determine the uniform large-alphabet minimax frontier indexed by near-tie mass and a tie atom.

method_exemplars.technique: Localize multivariate polynomial approximation to data-certified diagonal neighborhoods and use factorial moments there while retaining plug-in estimation away from ties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The margin condition weights exactly the nonsmooth region treated by the L1 estimator's diagonal polynomial, so its local risk proof can be reweighted by causal cell mass.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate localized sign alternatives to a margin exponent and prove matching plug-in upper and Assouad-type lower rates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same weighted small-contrast geometry controls which cells contribute max-functional bias and testing difficulty, though the destination target is value estimation rather than policy regret.

method_exemplars.technique: Use optimal-value influence-function analysis and an online one-step construction to separate exact exceptional laws from merely small nonzero gaps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It identifies the correct tie-atom regularity boundary that the proposed global minimax risk must retain rather than average away.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the minimax MSE and consistency frontier for the unrestricted discrete-confounder optimal value when armwise overlap weakens along a triangular array epsilon_n tending to zero.

source_refs.claim: Shows that point identification under weak support need not imply regular estimability and that treatment-effect rates depend on support-tail behavior.
source_refs.author: Shakeeb Khan, Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: Derives slower rates and non-Gaussian stable limits for treatment-effect estimators when propensity scores can be extreme.
source_refs.author: Phillip Heiler, Ekaterina Kazak

source_refs.claim: Formalizes why strict overlap becomes increasingly restrictive as covariate dimension and treatment-prediction accuracy grow.
source_refs.author: Alexander D'Amour, Peng Ding, Avi Feller, Lihua Lei, Jasjeet Sekhon

source_refs.claim: Studies discrete-cell causal minimax estimation under a fixed strong-overlap constant and does not provide a joint d-by-epsilon_n phase diagram.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.excerpt: After the fixed-epsilon frontier is resolved, formulate the epsilon_n-to-zero phase diagram
No uniform triangular-array lower phase or sharp overlap-varying constants are claimed.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Weak-overlap work treats smooth treatment-effect means through heavy inverse weights, while large-alphabet causal minimax theory fixes epsilon and optimal-value theory isolates tie nonregularity. For the oracle value, rare treatment-arm faces of the overlap cone intersect the max functional's tie diagonal. The first fixed-overlap proof step that fails is the uniform polynomial-coefficient and factorial-moment variance bound, whose constants diverge as epsilon_n shrinks; the lower prior must also hide its signed contrast in the rare arm without violating the triangular-array constraint. Thus neither the fixed-interior CausalSmith construction nor semiparametric weak-overlap asymptotics determines the joint n-d-epsilon_n frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching upper and lower risk bounds as an explicit function R(n,d,epsilon_n), identifying root-n, large-alphabet, weak-overlap, inconsistent, and zero-overlap boundary regimes and providing an overlap-adaptive estimator wherever adaptation is possible.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation cleanly separates formal point identification from practical estimability and makes support deterioration the driver of a statistical phase transition.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conditional exchangeability identifies the target -> identification may rely on increasingly rare treatment support -> weak support destroys regular estimation -> quantify that deterioration for a nonsmooth large-alphabet oracle value.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain epsilon_n explicitly in the Poissonized cell experiment, moment constraints, estimator variance, and fixed-sample fuzzy-prior transfer rather than absorbing it into constants.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the direct large-alphabet causal experiment, but its upper and lower calculations must be rebuilt to track vanishing arm probabilities.

method_exemplars.technique: Classify overlap regimes through propensity-tail behavior, derive nonstandard normalizations and stable limits, and use adaptive resampling for extreme-weight contributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the weak-overlap side of the phase diagram and shows concretely how overlap changes rates without changing the causal estimand.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate an absolute contrast on a nonsmooth bivariate region and control accumulated factorial-moment variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination requires the same diagonal treatment on anisotropic overlap cones whose widths and coefficient bounds now depend on epsilon_n.

open_problems.open_problem: For K treatments and d unrestricted discrete confounder cells, characterize the sharp minimax MSE of the oracle value sum_x p_x max_{a<=K} mu_ax when d and K may both grow under fixed armwise overlap.

source_refs.claim: Motivates many and combination treatments and proves value-reduction bounds under structured outcome models, not unrestricted oracle-value estimation.
source_refs.author: Qi Xu, Haoda Fu, Annie Qu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Treats expected maxima over a finite action set through softmax smoothing but does not derive large-alphabet minimax rates with both d and action count growing.
source_refs.author: Justin Whitehouse, Qizhao Chen, Morgane Austern, Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.claim: Solves the two-distribution absolute-difference functional using bivariate approximation and therefore supplies only the binary tie-face prototype.
source_refs.author: Jiantao Jiao, Yanjun Han, Tsachy Weissman

source_refs.excerpt: The binary optimal-policy value is nonsmooth at treatment-response ties.
The calibration uses a polynomial approximation of phi on the overlap-restricted four-cell cone

open_problems.why_unsolved: The binary maximum reduces to one absolute contrast, but K actions create a polyhedral tie fan with pairwise and higher-order intersections. Structured multi-action policy papers study regret or value reduction, while smoothing papers assume fixed action complexity and usable nuisance rates. The first binary proof step that changes is the approximation lemma: one bivariate diagonal polynomial must become a K-variate homogeneous approximation to the maximum over overlapping tie faces, including heavy cells near triple or higher ties, with factorial-moment variance controlled as K grows. The lower proof likewise needs a K-ary hidden-best-arm mixture that preserves armwise overlap, so a verbatim binary transfer cannot determine the K dependence.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided rate formula R(n,d,K,epsilon) with thresholds in both d and K, a computable tie-face-adaptive polynomial estimator, and a K-ary fuzzy-prior or Assouad converse identifying the active tie geometry.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates why multiple and combination treatments are scientifically distinct from a binary choice and clearly formulates the many-action decision geometry.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Modern interventions offer multiple or combinable actions -> individualized choice compares many conditional outcomes -> action interactions and partial ties complicate value analysis -> determine the unrestricted scalar oracle-value frontier when both strata and actions proliferate.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a near-diagonal multivariate polynomial estimator, lift its monomials with unbiased factorial moments, and prove risk using approximation and Poisson moment bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the binary tie-face prototype; the destination replaces one equality diagonal by the full K-action tie fan.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit derivative and bias properties of a softmax over finitely many causal scores and then orthogonalize the smoothed value score.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It handles the correct K-way maximum geometry and can guide the smooth-region estimator and the dependence on partial action gaps.

method_exemplars.technique: Use approximation duality to turn polynomial approximation error into moment-matched fuzzy-prior separation and a minimax lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A K-action converse needs this dual move after identifying a symmetric slice of the K-way maximum that preserves the observational constraints.

literature_map:
Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy (2024, arXiv:2405.00118) are the nearest causal minimax anchor: high-dimensional discrete confounders, fixed overlap, linear causal means and ATE, but no oracle maximum.
Luedtke and van der Laan (2016, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1603.07573) identify the optimal value's pathwise-differentiability boundary and make exact treatment-effect ties central.
Shi, Lu, and Song (2020, JMLR) use subagging for optimal-value inference under nonregularity, but do not give a growing-alphabet minimax characterization.
Whitehouse, Chen, Austern, and Syrgkanis (2025, arXiv:2507.11780) use softmax smoothing and gap conditions; their nuisance-rate regime does not resolve unrestricted d-cell occupancy.
Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman (2015, IEEE TIT, arXiv:1406.6956) establish the smooth-region plug-in/nonsmooth-region polynomial recipe for large-alphabet functionals.
Jiao, Han, and Weissman (2018, IEEE TIT, arXiv:1705.00807) are the closest method anchor: minimax L1-distance estimation requires multivariate approximation around an equality diagonal.
Wu and Yang (2016, IEEE TIT, arXiv:1407.0381) pair factorial-moment polynomial estimators with approximation-dual fuzzy priors and obtain an n log n threshold.
Cai and Low (2011, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1105.3039) provide composite-hypothesis and polynomial-expansion machinery for an L1-type nonsmooth functional.
Han, Jiao, and Weissman (2018, arXiv:1802.08405) develop computable local moment matching as an alternative implementation route.
Khan and Tamer (2010, Econometrica) show that weak support creates irregular estimability even under point identification; Heiler and Kazak (2021, Journal of Econometrics) connect extreme propensities to nonstandard rates and stable limits.
D'Amour, Ding, Feller, Lei, and Sekhon (2021, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1711.02582) explain why strict overlap becomes consequential in high-dimensional covariate settings.
Kitagawa and Tetenov (2018, Econometrica) give minimax regret theory for learned treatment rules, adjacent to but distinct from estimating the unrestricted scalar oracle value.
Xu, Fu, and Qu (2024, JRSSB, arXiv:2303.11507) treat many and combination treatments under structured models, leaving unrestricted K-way scalar-value minimax risk open.
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2203.00837) develop fuzzy-hypothesis causal minimax theory for smooth CATE estimation, not the discrete maximum functional.
The unoccupied intersection is large-alphabet causal ratio estimation plus a nonsmooth max/tie diagonal; no located paper supplies its sharp MSE frontier, diagonal-adaptive estimator, and matching causal fuzzy-prior lower bound.

Its reusable signal is the overlap-cone heavy/light ratio-polynomial construction; angle0_v2 explicitly requests an epsilon_n-to-zero phase diagram.
